findings.title: Delete menu item can never appear for Grafana rules in the list view (rulerRule is always undefined there)
findings.body: The Delete menu item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the alert list view the whole point of this PR is that no ruler API calls are made, so `RuleActionsButtons.V2` is rendered with only `promRule` and `rule` (rulerRule) is `undefined`. Even though the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` path can set `canDelete` to true from prom-rule/folder permissions, the `rulerRule &&` guard means the Delete item is never rendered in the list view, so users can no longer delete Grafana-managed rules from the list. The pause menu item at line 123 has the same problem: `canPause` can be true via the grafana ability, but rendering requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, which is false when only a promRule exists. Either the menu items need to work off the promRule (e.g. construct the delete/pause payloads from the prom rule), or the abilities should not report these actions as available.

findings.title: Silence menu item shown in list view but clicking it does nothing (drawer requires rulerRule)
findings.body: `AlertRuleMenu` will show 'Silence notifications' in the list view because the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` grants the Silence ability from the prom rule. Clicking it calls `handleSilence` which sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true, but the drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true — and `rule` (the ruler rule) is always undefined in the list view since this PR removes ruler requests there. Result: a visible menu action that silently does nothing. The silence flow needs to work from the prom rule (e.g. build the silence from promRule labels/uid) or the Silence ability should not be reported as supported when no ruler rule is available.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a React key in the filtered results list
findings.body: In the `origin === 'grafana'` branch the returned `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` no longer receives `key={key}` (the previous `GrafanaRuleLoader` had it). These elements are siblings of keyed `<DataSourceRuleLoader key={key}>` items inside the same `<ul>`, so React will warn about missing keys and, more importantly, reconciliation across pages of infinite-scroll results can reuse the wrong component instance for a different rule, showing stale state. Add `key={key}` to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` element.

findings.title: ModifyExport ability for prom rules excludes recording rules, unlike the ruler-rule path
findings.body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport` is `[isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` where `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. The equivalent ruler-based hook uses `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which matches both alerting and recording Grafana rules. So a Grafana-managed recording rule shows the Export menu in the details view (ruler path) but not in the list view (prom path). If export of recording rules is intended to remain available, use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` here; otherwise the two paths should be made consistent.

findings.title: Removed coverage for creating/deleting rule states with no replacement
findings.body: The PR deletes the tests 'should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists', 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists', and the entire `matchRules` describe block, and the component no longer has any creating/deleting handling. The behavior change (a just-created rule now simply doesn't appear until Prometheus catches up, and a deleting rule renders fully actionable until it disappears) is a real UX regression risk that is now completely untested — there is no test asserting what the list shows during these eventual-consistency windows.
